snippet.title: Learning Python for Cybersecurity
snippet.description:
I have recently been messing around with Python, creating some little "security projects." In this video, I talk about the three reasons why you should learn python for cybersecurity, when you should learn, and which resources you should use to learn. Description of each reason below


Why should I learn Python?
Reason #1: It's relatively easy
Reason #2: Modules and Extensive Library Access
Reason #3: Automation & Versatility

When should I learn Python? 

Whenever you have the time to learn. Set aside a few hours to learn the python basics and then move on to some "security-focused" projects after touching the basics. Make sure to complete any project before you learn python. Give the fundamentals your full attention.

Where should I learn Python?
For the python basics, I recommend looking up "free python 3 learning resources" and choosing one resource to learn from. Finish this resource until you are complete and then you can move into the cybersecurity projects. For security, I recommend two resources which are linked below.

snippet.title: What types of entry-level cybersecurity roles are there?
snippet.description:
There are several type of entry-level careers or roles in cybersecurity. As students in cybersecurity, I think it's important we expose ourselves to the different types of careers, even if we are just beginning out. I think it will help us understand where we want to go within the industry and what we want to do as we advance further into our studies.

I briefly outline the overall responsibilities and goal of each entry-level role in cybersecurity.

Today I talk about six types of entry-level roles:
- Security Analyst (2:00)
- Security Auditor (3:33)
- Security Specialist (4:37)
- Incident Responder (5:26)
- Penetration Tester / Ethical Hacker (6:23)
- Vulnerability Assessor (7:49)

These entry-level roles are common, but not limited to only six. 

Keep in mind, I am not an expert. Depending on the company, these entry-level roles may vary in titling.

snippet.title: Introduction to Linux for Cybersecurity Crash Course 2020
snippet.description:
If you are looking to introduce yourself to the Linux basics geared towards a cybersecurity perspective, you can use this brief crash course to learn. Read below for a further explanation behind why you should learn Linux if you are considering cybersecurity... 👇

Learning how to effectively navigate and interact with Linux can be an important part to your learning journey in cybersecurity. In this crash course, we walk through the very basics including how to configure your own Linux environment, navigate the command line, and apply our basic knowledge to a security use. 

You may be wondering... Why learn what we are learning? Why are we learning about how to change and create new directories, create new files, and file permissions...?

Part of the learning process before transitioning into the specific use cases for cybersecurity is learning the very basics. Once you get the basics down, you can start to apply your knowledge and run specific programs for security. This is why we start out with the very basics. 


If you have any questions, comments, or concerns, please leave a comment in the comment section or email me.
